newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey extends nuclear plant tender enquiry period.
newsitem.headline: Turkey extends nuclear plant tender enquiry period.

text.p: Turkey has extended the period for companies to request information on a tender for construction of the country's first nuclear power station, state-run Anatolian news agency reported.
"The period for taking the conditions has been extended at the request of some companies for ten days after it expired on Monday, January 20," the agency said of the Akkuyu plant tender.
It quoted officials from the state power utility company TEAS as saying the extension was agreed as only four companies had so far sought the tender conditions.
These four group's were Canada's AECL, the French-German venture NPI, Westinghouse -Mitsubishi and Italy's Ansaldo, Anatolian said.
It said General Electric Co Plc and ABB were also expected to request the tender conditions for the plant, to be located near the village of Akkuyu village on the Mediterranean.
Turkey's plans for a nuclear power plant were first put forward 30 years ago and have been revived as the country faces urgent pressure to stave off energy shortages in coming years.
TEAS is to collect bids by June 30 on the tender for which there are two options.

The first is a plant of one or more units with a capacity ranging from 900 MegaWatts (MW) to 1,400 MW. The other option's range is between 2,400 to 2,800 MW. Each power production unit in both options should have a capacity of 600 MW or more.
TEAS has said the plant would be fully financed by the builder on a turn-key basis and would cost about $1.5 to $2 billion depending on the option chosen.
